pairs: Dixerunt autem filii prophetarum ad Eliseum:
Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha:
Ecce locus in quo habitamus coram te,
the place in which we live before you is too narrow for us.
Let us go as far as the Jordan,
et tollant singuli de silva materias singulas,
and let us each take from the forest a piece of timber,
ut ædificemus nobis ibi locum ad habitandum.
so that we may build for ourselves a place to live there.”
And one of them said, “Then you,
Veni ergo et tu cum servis tuis.
too, should go with your servants.”
And when they had arrived at the Jordan,
Accidit autem ut cum unus materiam succidisset,
the iron of the ax fell into the water.
And he cried out and said:
Then the man of God said,
And he indicated to him the place.
Then he cut off a piece of wood,
Rex autem Syriæ pugnabat contra Israël,
Now the king of Syria was fighting against Israel,
and he took counsel with his servants,
let us set up an ambush.”
Misit itaque vir Dei ad regem Israël,
And so the man of God sent to the king of Israel,
Cave ne transeas in locum illum:
“Take care not to pass by that place.
quia ibi Syri in insidiis sunt.
For the Syrians are there in ambush.”
Misit itaque rex Israël ad locum quem dixerat ei vir Dei,
And so the king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God had told him, and he prevented it.
et observavit se ibi non semel neque bis.
concerning that place, not merely once or twice.
Conturbatumque est cor regis Syriæ pro hac re:
And the heart of the king of Syria was disturbed over this matter.
Quare non indicatis mihi quis proditor mei sit apud regem Israël?
“Why have you not revealed to me the one who is betraying me to the king of Israel?”
And one of his servants said:
sed Eliseus propheta qui est in Israël,
Rather it is the prophet Elisha, who is in Israel,
indicat regi Israël omnia verba quæcumque locutus fueris in conclavi tuo.
who is revealing to the king of Israel every word whatsoever that you will speak in your conclave.”
so that I may send and capture him.”
Misit ergo illuc equos et currus,
Therefore, he sent horses, and chariots,
and experienced soldiers to that place.
qui cum venissent nocte, circumdederunt civitatem.
And when they had arrived in the night, they encircled the city.
Consurgens autem diluculo minister viri Dei,
Now the servant of the man of God,
egressus vidit exercitum in circuitu civitatis,
went out and saw the army all around the city,
And he reported it to him,
But he responded: “Do not be afraid.
plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis.
For there are more with us than with them.”
And when Elisha had prayed, he said,
open the eyes of this one,
And the Lord opened the eyes of the servant,
et ecce mons plenus equorum et curruum igneorum in circuitu Elisei.
And behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire, all around Elisha.
Then truly, the enemies descended to him.
But Elisha prayed to the Lord,
And the Lord struck them, so that they would not see,
in accord with the word of Elisha.
and this is not the city.
et ostendam vobis virum quem quæritis.
and I will reveal to you the man whom you are seeking.”
Then he led them into Samaria.
And when they had entered into Samaria,
open the eyes of these ones,
And the Lord opened their eyes,
et viderunt se esse in medio Samariæ.
and they saw themselves to be in the midst of Samaria.
And the king of Israel, when he had seen them,
“My father, should I not strike them?”
And he said: “You should not strike them.
neque enim cepisti eos gladio et arcu tuo, ut percutias:
For you did not capture them with your sword or bow, so that you might strike them.
sed pone panem et aquam coram eis,
Instead, set bread and water before them,
so that they may eat and drink,
and then go to their lord.”
Appositaque est eis ciborum magna præparatio,
And a great preparation of foods was placed before them.
And they went away to their lord.
et ultra non venerunt latrones Syriæ in terram Israël.
And the robbers of Syria no longer came into the land of Israel.
Now it happened that, after these things,
congregavit Benadad rex Syriæ universum exercitum suum,
Benhadad, the king of Syria, gathered together his entire army,
and he ascended and was besieging Samaria.
Factaque est fames magna in Samaria:
And a great famine occurred in Samaria.
And it was blockaded for a long time,
donec venundaretur caput asini octoginta argenteis,
until the head of a donkey was sold for eighty pieces of silver,
et quarta pars cabi stercoris columbarum quinque argenteis.
and one fourth part of a pint of pigeons’ dung sold for five silver coins.
Cumque rex Israël transiret per murum,
And as the king of Israel was passing by the wall,
a certain woman cried out to him,
“If the Lord does not save you,
how am I able to save you?
And the king said to her,
so that we may eat him today,
and we will eat my son tomorrow.’
And I said to her on the next day,
so that we may eat him.’
When the king had heard this,
and he passed along the wall.
Viditque omnis populus cilicium quo vestitus erat ad carnem intrinsecus.
And all the people saw the haircloth that he had worn underneath, beside his flesh.
“May God do these things to me,
and may he add these other things,
si steterit caput Elisei filii Saphat super ipsum hodie.
if the head of Elisha, the son of Shaphat, will remain on him this day!”
Eliseus autem sedebat in domo sua,
Now Elisha was sitting in his house,
and the elders were sitting with him.
And so he sent a man ahead.
Numquid scitis quod miserit filius homicidæ hic, ut præcidatur caput meum?
“Do you not know that this son of a murderer is sending someone to cut off my head?
and when the messenger arrives, close the door.
And you shall not permit him to enter.
ecce enim sonitus pedum domini ejus post eum est.
For behold, the sound of his lord’s feet is behind him.”
While he was still speaking to them,
apparuit nuntius qui veniebat ad eum.
the messenger appeared who was sent to him.
such a great evil is from the Lord!
What more should I expect from the Lord?”
